applicability.scope: Deciding whether to write a custom inference kernel, routing a kernel pattern to Triton, CuTe DSL, CUDA C++, AscendC or TileIR, applying framework-independent correctness rules, and verifying the executing kernel against a reference before benchmarking; covers fused elementwise chains, reductions, tiled GEMM, attention variants, custom collectives, causal convolution and stateful serving-operator qualification
applicability.prerequisites: The applicable operator, caller/state and layout contracts are read before substitution, including the causal-conv1d contract and HF Qwen3.5 GDN binding; the CuTe DSL environment uses Linux x86_64, Python 3.10–3.13 and Ampere+ (SM80+) with nvidia-cutlass-dsl installed and no NPU target; the CANN programming guide for the specific SoC is consulted for AscendC
applicability.input_contract: The candidate operation or operation chain, its shapes, dtypes, quantization and layout requirements, and the target execution phase; the target accelerator and framework constraints; for serving operators, the concrete caller, effective phase and backend, state-row mapping, cache or buffer lifetime and in-place-write behavior; a reference implementation with the same signature, a callable kernel wrapper and fresh CUDA or NPU test tensors; verification shapes and dtypes plus profiler output for the target metric
applicability.produced_artifact: A write-or-decline decision for the candidate operation with the profiled bottleneck, fusable pair or required dtype, shape or quantization variant unsupported by the standard implementation that justifies it, a framework choice routed by pattern and accelerator, a correctness checklist covering fp32 transcendental round-trips, sync-free wrappers, C division semantics, pre-allocated outputs, fp32 matmul accumulators and masked boundary loads and stores, a starting block or tile size with its autotune and warmup cost noted, a kernel shipping kernel_fn, reference_fn and get_inputs, a reference-parity result across the verification shapes and dtypes, and a post-verification profiler reading on the target metric; for an existing causal-convolution or stateful serving operator, a qualification record naming the caller, phase, backend, state rows and in-place writes, with source selection kept apart from executed dispatch; a routing and correctness decision, not a complete implementation or a measured speedup
failure_modes: A kernel is written for a standalone elementwise op, a standalone matmul or standard attention where the vendor library already wins
Host-side scheduling cost is treated as a kernel problem instead of being routed to host-overhead-profiling
Fusion is justified by removed Python call overhead rather than by the DRAM traffic the shared data no longer makes
A transcendental runs on fp16/bf16 inputs without the fp32 cast round-trip, so the error stays silent through benchmarking
tl.dot accumulates in the input dtype because Triton is assumed to promote fp16/bf16 to fp32 automatically
Negative offsets are computed assuming Python floor division while Triton or AscendC rounds toward zero
An unmasked load or store is accepted because the benchmark shapes happen to divide the block size
A kernel is benchmarked before it matches its reference, or a shape-boundary, accumulator-dtype or precision failure is read as a tuning problem
A verification pass is reported as a win although the profiler metric did not move, so the kernel was never on the critical path
Autotune compile cost is measured as steady-state serving latency instead of being pre-warmed or cached
A CuTe DSL pattern is routed to an NPU target, or a CUDA tail-guard, attention primitive or SM-matched example is assumed to carry to Ascend
A causal-conv1d or GDN operator is substituted on build success, import success or matching names without resolving dtype, strides, packed boundaries, state rows and cursors
An in-tree vLLM wrapper, a GDN prefill flag or a cache-free classification adapter is read as establishing the executed convolution path or generation-state support
applicability.refusal_point: Declines to start a kernel until a profiler puts the target on the critical path near its hardware ceiling, a concrete fusable pair is identified, or the required dtype, shape or quantization variant is unsupported by the standard implementation, and sends host-bound cases elsewhere; refuses to benchmark an unverified kernel and withholds a gain whose profiler metric did not move; keeps operator source selection separate from executed dispatch, numerical parity and hardware qualification, so build or import success qualifies nothing; treats AscendC and TileIR content as source-inferred pending CANN and SoC verification with no local NPU run, treats the AKG Affine FileCheck expectations as IR structure rather than executed CUDA correctness, and reads author-reported overlap and FP8 cases as counterexamples to unconditional tuning rules; claims no Ascend support from NVIDIA primitives
applicability.hardware: CUDA Ampere+ and Ascend NPU have separate framework routes for each kernel pattern; CuTe DSL requires Linux x86_64, Python 3.10-3.13 and SM80+ with nvidia-cutlass-dsl and is unavailable on NPU; profiling uses ncu on CUDA and msprof on Ascend; the AscendC and TileIR guidance is source-inferred with no local NPU verification and requires validation against the specific CANN version and SoC

recommendations: Confirm with nsys/ncu or msprof that the target kernel sits on the critical path near its hardware ceiling, name the adjacent operations whose shared data would otherwise round-trip through DRAM, or identify a required dtype, shape or quantization variant unsupported by the standard implementation, before writing any kernel.

Ship every kernel with kernel_fn, reference_fn and get_inputs, pass reference parity across the verification shapes and dtypes first, and profile afterwards to confirm the target metric actually moved.
Cast fp16/bf16 to fp32 and back for any math beyond +, -, * and /, declare tl.dot accumulators as tl.float32, and mask every load and store whose shape does not divide the block size.

Start Triton at BLOCK_SIZE 1024 on Hopper and 512 on Ampere using powers of two, take GEMM tiles from the source skeleton configs (128/256/64 for Hopper, 64/128/32 for smaller cards) and autotune from there.
On Ascend, reach for TileIR before raw AscendC, size tiles to fit the AI Core Unified Buffer and check cube-unit alignment against the CANN guide for the specific SoC.

Match a CuTe DSL example to the GPU architecture (SM80 Ampere, SM90 Hopper, SM100 Blackwell) and study its structure instead of copying it, and pre-warm or cache autotuned kernels at startup so first-run compile cost stays out of serving latency.
